title: The Bug Nobody Wanted

pre.en: Why did Chen finally fix the bug?
pre.zh: 小陈最后为什么修了这个 bug？
options: Rachel ordered him to fix it.
A user's email made the bug feel important.
The bug started to appear on new phones.
Mia wrote down a new rule.

intro: 小陈讲一个拖了两周的小 bug：大家都看惯了，谁也不修，直到一位用户写来一封客气的邮件。读的时候留意 be used to doing（已经习惯）和 get used to doing（渐渐习惯）：这里的 to 是介词，后面跟 doing。结尾很短，却是整篇的重点。

sentences.en: For two weeks, our app had a bug that nobody was looking forward to fixing.
sentences.zh: 有两个星期，我们 App 里有个 bug，谁都不想去修。

sentences.en: It only appeared on old phones with an almost empty battery.
sentences.zh: 它只在电量快用完的旧手机上出现。

sentences.en: Every Monday, someone brought it up at stand-up, and we all agreed it was "not a priority".
sentences.zh: 每周一的站会上总有人提起它，大家也都同意它「不急」。

sentences.en: We were so used to seeing it on the list that nobody really noticed it any more.
sentences.zh: 我们早就看惯了它挂在清单上，谁都没再把它当回事。

sentences.en: Users were used to restarting the app, I told myself.
sentences.zh: 用户早就习惯重启 App 了，我这么安慰自己。

sentences.en: After all, it only takes ten seconds.
sentences.zh: 反正也就十秒钟的事。

sentences.en: Honestly, I'd got used to putting it off.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我也渐渐习惯了一拖再拖。

sentences.en: Then Rachel forwarded me a polite email from a user.
sentences.zh: 后来，Rachel 转给我一封用户的邮件，写得很客气。

sentences.en: She wasn't used to complaining, she wrote, but the app had crashed four times that morning.
sentences.zh: 她说自己不太习惯投诉，可那天上午 App 崩了四次。

sentences.en: She'd lost a long message to her son, who lives abroad.
sentences.zh: 她给在国外的儿子写的一条长消息也没了。

sentences.en: So I looked into it that afternoon.
sentences.zh: 那天下午我就去查了。

sentences.en: It took me three hours to track it down.
sentences.zh: 我花了三个小时才找到原因。

sentences.en: It was one line of code that ran out of memory in power-saving mode.
sentences.zh: 是一行代码，在省电模式下把内存用光了。

sentences.en: The fix took ten minutes.
sentences.zh: 修只用了十分钟。

sentences.en: Then I struck up a conversation with the man in the phone shop downstairs, and he lent me four old phones.
sentences.zh: 然后我跟楼下手机店的老板聊了起来，他借给我四部旧手机。

sentences.en: I double-checked the fix on all four.
sentences.zh: 我在四部手机上把修复后的效果都仔细测了一遍。

sentences.en: At stand-up, my mind nearly went blank, so I got straight to the point.
sentences.zh: 站会上我脑子差点一片空白，干脆直奔主题。

sentences.en: We agreed on a new rule, and Mia insisted on writing it down.
sentences.zh: 我们商定了一条新规矩，Mia 非要把它写下来。

sentences.en: Any bug that's been on the list for more than a week has to be dealt with first.
sentences.zh: 在清单上挂了一周以上的 bug，都得先处理。

sentences.en: Looking back, the hardest part wasn't the code.
sentences.zh: 回头看，最难的不是代码。

sentences.en: It was admitting that "not a priority" really meant "not my problem".
sentences.zh: 而是承认：「不急」其实就是「不关我的事」。

sentences.en: Anyway, I wrote back to that user and kept checking my inbox.
sentences.zh: 总之，我给那位用户回了信，然后一直刷收件箱。

sentences.en: She replied the next day: "Thank you. My son says hi."
sentences.zh: 第二天她回复了：「谢谢你。我儿子向你问好。」

cards.note: to feel happy about something that is going to happen
to start talking about a subject
cards.tip: 代词放中间：bring it up，不说 bring up it。另一个意思是「抚养」：She was brought up in Leeds。
cards.example: I'll bring it up at the next team meeting.

cards.note: top priority 头等大事；工作里说 not a priority，常常是「先放着」的委婉说法。

cards.text: It takes sb + 时间 + to do
cards.note: used to say how much time someone needs to do something
to decide to do something later than planned
cards.tip: 代词要放中间：put it off；后面接动作用 doing：put off calling the bank。
cards.example: Don't put off the code review until Friday.

cards.note: complain about sth 抱怨某事；名词 complaint（第 29 课）。
abroad 是副词，前面不加介词：live abroad、go abroad，不说 go to abroad。
to try to find out the facts about a problem
cards.tip: 和 look at 不同：look at 是「看」，look into 是「深入查原因」；代词放在后面：look into it。
cards.example: Can you look into why the build failed?

cards.note: to find something or someone after searching for a long time
cards.tip: 代词放中间：track it down；强调找得辛苦，找 bug、找人都能用。
cards.example: It took us a week to track down the cause of the crash.

cards.note: to use all of something so that none is left
cards.tip: 人或物做主语都行，后面接用完的东西；不接宾语时去掉 of：The memory ran out。
cards.example: We've run out of coffee in the office.

cards.note: 电脑和手机的「内存」也是 memory；人的「记性」也是：I have a bad memory。
手机电量低时打开的模式；也说 low power mode。

cards.zh: （和陌生人）攀谈起来；搭起话来
cards.note: to start talking to someone you don't know
to check something again to make sure it is correct
cards.tip: 做动词，后面直接接要核对的东西；名词说 do a double-check。
cards.example: Can you double-check the date before you send the invite?

cards.note: if your mind goes blank, you suddenly cannot remember or think of anything
cards.tip: 主语常是 my mind / my head；屏幕变黑也能说 the screen went blank。
cards.example: When the interviewer asked my first question, my mind went blank.

cards.note: to start talking or writing about the most important thing
cards.tip: straight 放在 to 前面加强语气：get straight to the point，直接说重点。
cards.example: I'll get to the point: we need two more developers.

cards.note: to decide something together after discussing it
cards.tip: agree on 某件事；agree with 某人；agree to do 同意去做。
cards.example: We couldn't agree on a name for the project.

cards.note: to say firmly that you will do something, or that something must happen
to take action to solve a problem or finish a task
cards.tip: 过去式和过去分词都是 dealt，读 /delt/；被动是 be dealt with，with 不能丢。
cards.example: I'll deal with the emails after lunch.

cards.note: used when you think about something that happened in the past
cards.tip: 常放句首，后面加逗号；常和 should have 连用，说当初该怎么做。
cards.example: Looking back, I should have asked for help earlier.

cards.note: admit doing / admit that …：承认自己做了（不太光彩的）事。
